description: A benchmark evaluating LLM agents on neuroimaging tasks. Platform-agnostic: tasks specify a scientific goal, a public dataset, and a ground-truth reference; agent outputs are graded against the reference.

schema.structure: Tasks nested within category divisions; flat within each category.

categories.data-handling: Converting and organizing raw data into standard formats (DICOM->BIDS, DICOM->NIfTI).
categories.structural: Anatomical T1w/T2w analysis: reconstruction, segmentation, morphometry, registration.
categories.functional: fMRI processing: preprocessing, denoising, connectivity, activity metrics.
categories.diffusion: Diffusion MRI: preprocessing, tensor/FOD modeling, tractography, connectomes.
categories.clinical: Clinical/pathology workflows: lesion and subfield segmentation, clinical preprocessing.
categories.electrophysiology: EEG/MEG processing (property-graded; no external ground truth).

agent_grader_split.prompt: AGENT-VISIBLE. goal (scientific WHAT only), dataset (identity), required_output (artifact + format so it is gradable, not how). required_tool only if the task is intrinsically named.
agent_grader_split.solution: GRADER-ONLY, never shown to agent. ground_truth (+location), metric, pass_criterion, tool_mode, tool_suggestions (NON-BINDING - agents may use novel/future tools), notes.

schema.tool_philosophy: Tools are SUGGESTIONS, never gate grading, EXCEPT intrinsically-named tasks (tool_mode=named) where the tool is part of the goal. Grading is always output-vs-ground-truth, so novel/future tools that produce correct output pass.
schema.anti_gaming: Enforced by the SCORER (not per-task): (1) artifact must exist with correct shape/format [catches no-op/fabrication], (2) artifact must be structurally valid [mask binary, matrix symmetric], (3) artifact must match hidden ground truth by metric [catches wrong-but-plausible]. Ground truth is hidden from agents. required_output per task anchors the existence/shape check.

clinical_motion_t1.notes: Markerless prospective motion-correction study (Cimbi). 22 HEALTHY ADULTS (19-36y). Multi-contrast: 3D T1 MPRAGE (22), FLAIR (10), T1 STIR (22), T2 TSE (22), T2* GRE (19), DWI (10, under derivatives). Each sequence acquired as still + nod (+ shake for T1) deliberate-motion variants. NOT pediatric, NOT longitudinal. MOTION-TASK POTENTIAL: the still/nod/shake structure makes this a strong candidate for motion-robustness / motion-QC tasks not yet in the benchmark

structural-brain-extraction.title: Brain extraction (skull stripping)
structural-brain-extraction.description: Skull-strip the T1w of {subject} of OpenNeuro dataset ds002790, producing a brain-extracted image and a binary brain mask in native T1w space.

prompt.goal: Skull-strip the T1-weighted image of {subject}, producing a brain-extracted image and a binary brain mask in the native T1w space.
prompt.required_output:
A skull-stripped brain image (NIfTI) and a binary brain mask (NIfTI) in native T1w space.

OUTPUT LOCATION (exact, mandatory): write your results into `submissions/structural-brain-extraction/{subject}/` under your working directory — create that folder. Put the binary brain mask at `submissions/structural-brain-extraction/{subject}/output.nii.gz` (THIS is the graded file) and the skull-stripped image at `submissions/structural-brain-extraction/{subject}/stripped.nii.gz`. Use these exact paths and filenames, and place no other NIfTI inside `submissions/structural-brain-extraction/{subject}/`. Only `submissions/structural-brain-extraction/{subject}/output.nii.gz` is scored.
prompt.subject_note: This task runs once per case. Its subjects are listed as cases in cases.json of the gated reference dataset; the harness fetches each one under its case id, and {subject} in the goal and the output paths is replaced with that id.

solution.ground_truth: STAPLE consensus of a panel of independent skull-strippers, split into core/margin/background zones and calibrated per subject; native T1w space. consensus_mask.nii.gz + consensus_zones.nii.gz in the Hugging Face dataset neurodeskorg/skills-comm-ground-truth, fetched into the grader pack reference/ at grade time.
solution.ground_truth_location: Hugging Face neurodeskorg/skills-comm-ground-truth (revision e3619b09778a), path structural_gt/structural-brain-extraction/{subject}/ (consensus_mask.nii.gz, consensus_zones.nii.gz)
solution.pass_criterion: A skull-stripped brain image and a binary brain mask are produced; Mask geometry (dimensions, voxel size, affine) matches the input image; Brain mask is binary (values 0 and 1 only); Brain mask is anatomically plausible: skull/dura removed, brain retained; No processing errors; logs captured
solution.output_validation: Run the grader (see the grader block); a submission passes when verdict >= acceptable (quality >= 60), which is how the reporting layer scores it. The script's exit code signals validity (no gate failure), not pass.

grader.description: Scores the mask against a STAPLE consensus of a panel of tools, split into core (must keep) / margin (free, not scored) / background (must exclude); all thresholds (tolerance tau, per-metric envelope, gate caps) are calibrated by leave-one-tool-out. See PROVENANCE.md for the calibration procedure.
grader.returns: JSON: verdict in {within_reference_variability, acceptable, marginal, unacceptable, invalid}, quality 0-100, gate_failures[], metrics{}
grader.pass_criterion: verdict >= acceptable (quality >= 60); the scorer's exit code signals validity (no gate failure), not pass

solution.tool_note: Context: healthy adult T1w. Any competent skull-stripper is a reasonable choice. Tool names are non-binding suggestions.

structural-mni-registration.title: MNI registration (T1w to MNI152NLin2009cAsym)
structural-mni-registration.description: Register the T1w of {subject} of OpenNeuro ds002790 to MNI152NLin2009cAsym and carry the supplied tissue segmentation through the same transform, graded by propagated-label overlap against the template's own tissue priors.

prompt.goal:
Register the T1-weighted image of {subject} to the MNI152NLin2009cAsym template and resample it into that space. Apply the SAME transform to the supplied tissue segmentation, using nearest-neighbour interpolation so its labels are preserved.

DATA. The subject images come from OpenNeuro ds002790 (tag 2.0.0):
  mkdir -p input template
  datalad clone https://github.com/OpenNeuroDatasets/ds002790.git ds002790
  git -C ds002790 checkout 2.0.0
  datalad -C ds002790 get {subject}/anat/{subject}_T1w.nii.gz \
      derivatives/fmriprep/{subject}/anat/{subject}_dseg.nii.gz
  cp -L ds002790/{subject}/anat/{subject}_T1w.nii.gz input/T1w.nii.gz
  cp -L ds002790/derivatives/fmriprep/{subject}/anat/{subject}_dseg.nii.gz input/dseg.nii.gz

The template is MNI152NLin2009cAsym at 1 mm (TemplateFlow), 193x229x193:
  curl -sSL --retry 3 https://templateflow.s3.amazonaws.com/tpl-MNI152NLin2009cAsym/tpl-MNI152NLin2009cAsym_res-01_T1w.nii.gz -o template/T1w.nii.gz

input/dseg.nii.gz is a tissue segmentation of that same T1w, with labels 1 = grey matter, 2 = white matter, 3 = CSF. Warp it with the transform you compute for the T1w; do not re-segment, and do not relabel it.

Both outputs must be on the template grid: the same shape and affine as template/T1w.nii.gz. Do not resample to any other space.
prompt.required_output:
The T1w resampled into MNI152NLin2009cAsym, and the tissue segmentation carried through the same transform with nearest-neighbour interpolation.

OUTPUT LOCATION (exact, mandatory): write your results into `submissions/structural-mni-registration/{subject}/` under your working directory - create that folder. Put the warped T1w at `submissions/structural-mni-registration/{subject}/output.nii.gz` and the warped segmentation at `submissions/structural-mni-registration/{subject}/dseg.nii.gz`. Use these exact paths and filenames, and place no other NIfTI inside `submissions/structural-mni-registration/{subject}/`. Both files are scored.
prompt.subject_note: This task runs once per case. Its subjects are listed as cases in cases.json of the gated reference dataset; the harness fetches each one under its case id, and {subject} in the goal and the output paths is replaced with that id.

solution.ground_truth: The template's own tissue priors (TemplateFlow MNI152NLin2009cAsym res-01 label-{GM,WM,CSF}_probseg), which state where each tissue belongs in MNI space independently of any registration software - not another tool's warp. A population prior is not a per-subject truth, so the thresholds are relative: the envelope is the spread achieved on that subject by several independent nonlinear registrations. Affine-only registration is the scored failure candidate and anchors zero credit.
solution.ground_truth_location: Hugging Face neurodeskorg/skills-comm-ground-truth (revision e3619b09778a), path structural_gt/structural-mni-registration/ (template_T1w.nii.gz, template_brain_mask.nii.gz, template_probseg_GM.nii.gz, template_probseg_WM.nii.gz, template_probseg_CSF.nii.gz)
solution.metric: prior-calibrated: verdict {within_reference_variability|acceptable|marginal|unacceptable|invalid} + weighted quality 0-100 from propagated-label Dice (WM, GM, CSF), brain overlap and in-brain image correlation (see grader)
solution.pass_criterion: A warped T1w and a warped tissue segmentation, both on the MNI152NLin2009cAsym grid; segmentation labels preserved (1/2/3, nearest-neighbour); brain lands where MNI expects it; propagated tissue overlap at least as good as the weakest independent nonlinear registration; No processing errors; logs captured
solution.output_validation: Run the grader (see the grader block); a submission passes when verdict >= acceptable (quality >= 60), which is how the reporting layer scores it. The script's exit code signals validity (no gate failure), not pass.

grader.description: Scores propagated-label overlap, not image similarity: the subject's own tissue segmentation is carried through the agent's transform and compared with the template's tissue priors. Weighted quality over WM Dice (0.30), GM Dice (0.25), brain Dice (0.20), in-brain correlation (0.15) and CSF Dice (0.10), each mapped by the envelope of four independent independent nonlinear registrations. Image correlation alone is nearly saturated after any affine and would not separate affine from nonlinear; WM Dice does. See PROVENANCE.md.
grader.pass_criterion: verdict >= acceptable (quality >= 60); the scorer's exit code signals validity (no gate failure), not pass

solution.tool_note: Context: healthy adult T1w at 1 mm, whole head, to MNI152NLin2009cAsym. Tool names are non-binding suggestions.
solution.notes: [note] First non-mask output type in the benchmark: the graded object is a spatial transform, observed through the image and segmentation it produces. [note] Runtime is not a barrier; the slowest package in the calibration build finished well inside a 45-minute agent budget. [caution] The segmentation is an agent INPUT, not a reference; it is supplied so the transform can be measured by label propagation. solution.output_validation: Run the grader (see the grader block); a submission passes when verdict >= acceptable (quality >= 60), which is how the reporting layer scores it. The script's exit code signals validity (no gate failure), not pass.

grader.description: Scores a binary mask against the STAPLE consensus in three zones: unanimous core (must be kept), margin (tools legitimately disagree, never scored) and background (must be excluded). The discriminating gate is no_focal_core_loss, a lost region that survives a shave of 1.5 mm or one voxel, whichever is larger: threshold-based methods drop the cerebellum on the raw b0 and fail it. See PROVENANCE.md.
